headline.tier: 🎉🎉 320-concept sparse-distributed G.20 ensemble — SHIPPED (98.4% per-bridge, ensemble validated)
headline.result: Production scaling target reached: 5 bridges x 64 sparse-distributed concepts = 320 unique concepts. Per-bridge discrimination 98.4% (uniform 63/64 all 5 bridges; one deterministic, characterized, seed-42-pattern-specific gap at concept index 12 -- NOT vocab-dependent, NOT simple overlap). Ensemble integration validated end-to-end seed 42: cross-bridge memory (apple is big -> 'apple' returns 'big' #1 at 779 vs ~658 noise), exact tag match, and -- critically -- the +160 EXTENSION vocab works: querying new word 'horse' retrieves both sentence co-members ('run' 882, 'fast' 508) cross-bridge across 3 bridges; role queries 100%. The 160-concept tier (2026-05-15) remains 100% per-bridge; 320 trades a characterized 1.6% per-bridge gap for 2x vocab. Multi-bridge scaling route confirmed linear in bridge count.
headline.metrics: 320 concepts, per-bridge 315/320 = 98.4% top-1 (deterministic idx-12 gap, seed-42 pattern-set artifact; idx-8/17 overlap more yet pass, so not raw overlap; cheap fix = per-bridge seeds / overlap-rejection, deferred). Ensemble demo seed 42: base + extension-vocab cross-bridge retrieval clears noise (779 vs 658; 882 vs 518); tag routing exact (A66 B65 C66 D64 E64). 41 vocab-spec tests + 16 sparse-mode tests + 141 G.20 tests green.
headline.wall_clock: 320 chain: ~34 min/bridge x 5 = ~2.8 hr (sparse-64, 25600 events/bridge, GPU-vectorized prior 0.2s). End-to-end 320 demo ~3.5 min.
headline.summary: 320-concept sparse-distributed conversational ensemble SHIPPED 2026-05-16 (production scaling target, ~age-5 vocab breadth). 5 bridges x 64 Kanerva-SDM concepts; 98.4% per-bridge (honest: not 100% like the 32-tier -- one characterized seed-42 idx-12 gap/bridge); cross-bridge memory + N-word sentences + role queries validated incl. the +160 extension vocab. Next: per-bridge seeds / overlap-rejection to recover toward 64/64; multi-seed ensemble.

pillars.name: ðŸŽ‰ðŸŽ‰ðŸŽ‰ Sparse-distributed G.20 64-concept at 100% PASS (true Kanerva form, 2026-05-15)
pillars.metric: After contiguous-slice 60-concept hit a wall at 78.3% top-1, pivoted to TRUE Kanerva-style sparse-distributed encoding (random sparse patterns, not contiguous blocks). Result: 64/64 (100%) top-1, 64/64 (100%) top-5 at seed 42 in 2000-neuron pool with 100-neuron sparse patterns. MORE concepts (64 vs 60), LESS substrate (2000 vs 3200), PERFECT discrimination (vs 78.3% / 96.7%). Architecture pivot validated. The contiguous-slice approximation was the bottleneck at 60+; sparse-distributed unlocks linear scaling. Capacity implications: 5-bridge sparse-distributed at 64/bridge = 320 concepts (vs current 160); at 128/bridge (testing) = 640 concepts. Combined with expanded morpheme dict (~10x reach): 3200-6400 surface forms = mid-child to early-adult vocabulary range. Catalog G.20 (Pulvermuller distributed cortical word ensembles): 'SAME NEURONS PARTICIPATE' specification now properly implemented via overlapping random patterns.

pillars.name: 60-word multi-bridge ensemble + 11 conversational features (5-seed VALIDATED 2026-05-15)
pillars.metric: 5 v16 bridges (set1-5) each owning 12 distinct concept words, routed by dispatch layer. FULL 5-SEED VALIDATION (seeds 42-46) for 4 new sets: 238/320 = 74.4% combined Phase 1 PASS rate, mean per-bridge 11.9/16 Â± 0.7 -- statistically indistinguishable from v16 baseline (12.4/16 Â± 1.52). 19 robust words (PASS at ALL 5 seeds), 45 fragile, 0 fail. End-to-end demo validates 11 features: pair encoding, N-word sentences, negation, conjunctions, possessives, pronoun coreference, tense (PAST/FUTURE), comparisons, yes/no, role queries, relational queries, memory CRUD. 91 unit tests pass (1.2s CPU). Total bridge state: 5 seeds * 4 sets * 25MB + 1 set1 = ~525 MB. Per-seed wall clock ~72 min for 4 new sets. Full 5-seed wall clock: ~6.3 hours total.

pillars.name: Multi-tag cue retrieval - 90% FULL, 100% PARTIAL multi-seed (real semantic conversation)
pillars.metric: v16 5-seed 8-cue: 36/40 = 90% FULL (all associates in top-2 of 15), 40/40 = 100% PARTIAL (any associate in top-2). Chance ~0.95% for FULL (2/15 * 1/14). Mechanism: for cue X, stim every engram tag containing X (each at 87.5% reliability), aggregate lang_output cosines, rank associates. User-friendly: types plain word, gets back all trained associates. Implemented in compose_concept_chat.py as default mode.

pillars.name: Multi-tag capacity - 98.8% PRECISION at 20 pairs encoded multi-seed
pillars.metric: v16 5-seed 20-pair 8-cue top-4: 158/160 = 98.8% PRECISION (every retrieved associate is a genuine trained binding). 20 pairs with 5-6 associates per cue exceeds top-4 capacity so FULL drops to 12.5%, but PRECISION stays at 98.8%. The system holds 20+ concept-concept associations cleanly; user needs 'tell me more' to enumerate all associates per cue. Practical capacity bound for conversational chat.

pillars.name: Compositional intersection ('what is a and b') - 90% FULL multi-seed
pillars.metric: v16 5-seed 4-query: 18/20 = 90% FULL (all shared associates in top-3), 20/20 = 100% PARTIAL. Tests compositional reasoning: drive cues a and b separately, intersect top-N associates, return shared. Test config: (apple, cat) both bound to (big, hot); (dog, river) both bound to (small, cold). Mechanism layered on top of validated multitag.

pillars.name: Yes/no questions ('is a b?') - 96.7% accuracy multi-seed
pillars.metric: v16 5-seed 6 TRUE + 6 NEGATIVE queries: 28/30 TP + 30/30 TN = 58/60 = 96.7%. PERFECT true negatives (system never falsely confirms untrained pair). 93.3% true positives (occasional 'PARTIAL' on weak recall). Strongest multi-seed metric in the conversational suite. Combines tag-existence check (deterministic) with stim-recall confidence verification.

pillars.name: Subject-verb-object role queries - 100% multi-seed
pillars.metric: v16 5-seed 8 sentences x 2 queries = 80 total: 80/80 = 100% role accuracy. Plus 35/40 = 87.5% neural verification (engram contains all 3 words). Sentences encoded as 3-word triples with tag name preserving order ('alice_stop_apple' vs 'apple_stop_alice'). Queries 'who V B?' and 'what did A V?' return correct subject/object via pattern match on tag names + neural stim verification. Distinguishes word order; this is genuine sentence-level conversation at v16 16-word vocab. Storage: engram tagging (catalog D.14); indexing: tag names; verification: stim-recall.

pillars.name: Engram-tag stim-recall - 87.5% multi-seed (catalog D.14 Tonegawa)
pillars.metric: v16 5-seed 8-pair: 35/40 = 87.5% stim-recall (both concepts in lang_output top-5). Range 6-8 per seed (75-100%). Chance baseline ~8.3% (5/16 * 4/15). Recipe: v16 baseline arch + 500 encoding events + balanced teacher 500 pA. Engram tag captures co-firing concept-pool neurons; stimulating tag reliably reactivates both concepts.

pillars.name: TRANSITIVE SEMANTIC INFERENCE - 90% (RETRACTED) - re-measured at 45% via multitag soft traversal
pillars.metric: RETRACTED: previous claim of 18/20 chained 90% was architecture-mismatch artifact. HONEST RE-MEASUREMENT 2026-05-14 PM via multitag mechanism (multitag_transitive_eval.py): 9/20 = 45% multi-seed transitive (chance 33%, so ~36% above chance). Direct (B in top-5): 95% multi-seed. Soft graph traversal is real but much weaker than originally claimed. The 'transitive inference' label was overstated; the actual capability is SOFT 2nd-degree neighbor retrieval at small cosine scores. Forensic on 20-pair test confirmed 2nd-degree neighbors appear in spurious retrievals (cat->cold->river pattern).

pillars.name: Concept-Concept Pool-Firing Readout - 65% (RETRACTED 2026-05-14)
pillars.metric: RETRACTED: previous 26/40 (65%) via pool-firing rank was an architecture-mismatch artifact. Re-test with corrected bridge (compose_concept_engram no longer monkey-patches v17 vocab): v16/v18/v19 all give 0/8 top-1 strict on seed 42 (vs claimed 2/8 = 25%). Cross-pool weights at 200 encoding events don't influence pool firing strongly enough to differentiate concept associations from random pool-firing biases.

pillars.name: Under-recall remediation: end-to-end validated, modest (+3.3pp)
pillars.metric: Artifact-safe boosted re-capture: 5/5 bridges had 1 under-recaller (idx-12), all fixed (161->1361, rank 20->1). End-to-end CONTROLLED: cross-bridge 80.0%->83.3% (+3.3pp, +1/6 misses recovered). Real+safe+production-foldable but MODEST -- under-recall is a partial contributor; majority of cross-bridge misses are a distinct still-open sub-mechanism (self-winning concepts that still lose cross-bridge). Not overclaimed as a cap fix.

pillars.name: Distinct cross-bridge sub-mechanism characterized (same-bridge cross-talk)
pillars.metric: Pure analysis of 10 cross-bridge misses (both 320 benchmarks): 50% SAME-AS-QUERY cross-talk (query bridge home-advantage in un-normalized max-rate aggregation), 40% THIRD-bridge spurious, 10% same-as-target. Points to a 2nd artifact-safe query-time lever (per-bridge rate normalization / same-bridge down-weight). Honest: 50% plurality not majority; 40% secondary unaddressed by that lever.

pillars.name: Artifact-safe levers (multi-seed refined): remediation robust, aggregation seed-variant
pillars.metric: Under-recall remediation: ROBUST +3.3pp (5/5 bridges, mechanism-deterministic) -> ship as default. samebridge_downweight: multi-seed (43-46) mean +2.5pp but 1/4 REGRESSED (-3.3pp seed43); SEED-VARIANT, not robust -> optional/tunable only, NOT default. perbridge_norm FALSIFIED (-16.7pp). Earlier seed-42 +6.7pp stacked down-graded honestly to ~+5pp-typical-but-variable. Multi-seed rigor caught the seed-42-favorable snapshot.

capacity_rule.rule: REVISED 2026-05-10: encoding-axis architecture recommended for vocab >= 32. Motor capacity matters less than encoding capacity at higher vocab tiers. Encoding (n_lang_input) is rate-limiting; motor pool just needs ~125 neurons/sub-pop to support STDP convergence.
